californiaFinding.verdict: Neither of the two answers step 2 offers is correct for California. The packet-ready outcome is NOT legally unavailable to a self-help participant, and the missing fact is NOT a legal precondition. California is closed by a shared escalation reacting to four OPTIONAL, route-specific Proposition 64 questions that a non-marijuana participant correctly answers 'I'm not sure'.

rootCause.mechanism: ambiguityReason escalates to needs_review with <code>.source_fact_unknown whenever ANY rendered, non-contextOnly, prepay question carries an explicit-unknown answer. It does not check whether the question belongs to the route the participant is on.
rootCause.californiaSpecificInput: CA publishes ca_prop64_qualifying_marijuana_offense, ca_prop64_lesser_or_no_offense, ca_prop64_branch and ca_prop64_relief_requested as prepay, non-contextOnly, required:false questions. The last two are text_or_unknown, so 'I'm not sure' is an explicit-unknown value.
observedReasonChain: with the audit's own answer set: ca.source_fact_unknown — 'ca_prop64_branch is uncertain and requires source review'
clearing only ca_prop64_branch: ca.source_fact_unknown — 'ca_prop64_relief_requested is uncertain and requires source review'

proof.method: replay of all eight recorded CA remedy contexts at this base, changing only the four ca_prop64_* answers from their explicit-unknown values to definite ones

result.remedyContext: Tool 4 — Arrest-record sealing (PC 851.91; factual innocence PC 851.8)

proof.conclusion: California has at least two packet-ready, payable routes behind this gate. The bounded sweep cannot reach them because it answers optional text questions with the unknown affordance, which is exactly what a participant with a non-marijuana record would do.

findings.AZ: Closed by Phase 2 and still closed at this base. The bounded sweep reaches packet_ready_with_caution on remedy-1-record-sealing; the remedy-context replay reproduces Phase 2's recorded proof byte-for-byte. No legal question remains open for AZ under this issue.
findings.MT: Same. packet_ready_with_caution on misdemeanor-conviction-expungement-under-mont-code-46-18-1104, replay byte-identical to the Phase 2 proof. No legal question remains open for MT under this issue.
findings.CA: Open. See step2.californiaFinding. The legal question for counsel is narrow and specific, and is NOT 'is a California packet available to a self-help participant' — the evidence says it is, on two routes. The question is: are the four ca_prop64_* facts legal preconditions for the five non-Proposition-64 California routes, or are they route-specific to the two § 11361.8 routes only? If the latter — which the compiled decision rules already say, since only the two prop-64 routes name them in requiredFields — then California's closure is a configuration defect, not a legal position, and the product is currently telling every Californian with a non-marijuana record that we need one more detail before we can prepare the right packet, when we do not.

waitingRuleDispositionSummary.rule: No fallback-dependent route is recommended ACTIVE. Every one of the 31 still resolves through the provisional prose selector at this base.

CA:prop-64-completed-sentence-applicatio.why: California is HELD_FOR_CORRECTION at the product base and this shard's prompt repeats the hold: 'Their pre-correction behaviour is preserved exactly.' A binding proposal for a California route would be a proposal to move a held jurisdiction's behaviour. The correction California needs first is the one recorded at step2Reachability.californiaFinding: while every California route escalates on an unknown Proposition 64 answer, no California route reaches its waiting rule at all, so which rule governs is not yet a live question.
CA:prop-64-completed-sentence-applicatio.correctionRequiredFirst: scope the ca_prop64_* facts to the two HSC § 11361.8 routes, or scope the shared ambiguityReason to the matched route's own fields

CA:tool-1-dismissal-set-aside.why: Same hold. Materially: with the four ca_prop64_* answers made definite, this route returns packet_ready_with_caution with paymentAllowed true at this base via ca.compiled_rule_match.rule-02. It is one of the two California routes the correction would reopen, which is exactly why its waiting rule must be settled after the correction and not before.

CA:tool-2-automatic-relief.why: Same hold. With the Proposition 64 answers made definite this route returns guidance_only (ca.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition) — a non-filing route, where a waiting-period binding may not be the right instrument at all. That is a question for after the correction.

CA:tool-3-petition-based-felony-sealing.why: Same hold. This is the one California route that, once the Proposition 64 gate is cleared, reaches its waiting rule and fails it: it returns needs_review with ca.waiting_rule_not_executed. So this route has a genuine, separate waiting-rule gap underneath the held correction. Recorded here rather than resolved: proposing a binding for it now would be proposing to move a held jurisdiction.
CA:tool-3-petition-based-felony-sealing.correctionRequiredFirst: same as above, then a binding for the SB 731 / PC 1203.49 framework

CA:tool-4-arrest-record-sealing.why: Same hold. With the Proposition 64 answers made definite this route returns packet_ready_with_caution with paymentAllowed true via ca.compiled_rule_match.rule-15. It is the second route the correction would reopen. It is also one of the two non-conviction routes UX-LEGAL-001 asks counsel about, so its exclusion and timing treatment is an open legal question in its own right.

CA:tool-5-proposition-64-marijuana-relie.why: Same hold. This route is categorised product_scope_exclusion and returns guidance_only under ca.lawrence_hold_guidance_only once the gate is cleared. A waiting-rule binding for a route the product does not sell is not the correction it needs.

MT:deferred-sentence-dismissal-or-confid.why: Every waiting-period row the prose selector can see for this route is the five-year clean period of the § 46-18-1104 MISDEMEANOR CONVICTION petition (wait-01, wait-02, wait-05, wait-06, wait-08), plus wait-04, which is the Montana DOJ's ~30-day CRISS PROCESSING time after an order is granted. Neither is this route's rule. The only thing the profile says about this route's timing is the table line 'Deferred sentence Dismissal can make records confidential', which states no period. Importing another route's five-year period, or treating a post-order processing latency as an eligibility wait, would both be authoring.

candidatesConsidered.quote: Five-year clean period Five years must have passed since completion of sentence terms.
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: this is the § 46-18-1104 misdemeanor-conviction period, already bound to MT:misdemeanor-conviction-expungement-under-mont-code-46-18-1104

candidatesConsidered.quote: DOJ says to allow about 30 days for processing.
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: processing latency after the court grants the order, not an eligibility waiting period

MT:deferred-sentence-dismissal-or-confid.whatCounselMustDecide: Does the § 46-18-204 deferred-sentence dismissal / confidentiality route carry an eligibility waiting period, and if so from what anchor?

MT:doj-record-removal-update-request.why: routeType administrative. The candidates are wait-04 (~30 days of DOJ CRISS processing), the § 46-18-1104 five-year rows, and a 21-day county-attorney opposition window carried in the pathway prose. None of the three is an eligibility waiting period for an administrative DOJ record-removal request. The profile states no period for this route.

candidatesConsidered.quote: DOJ says to allow about 30 days for processing.
the person has had no convictions in Montana, another state, or federal court for five years after completing the sentence terms

MT:doj-record-removal-update-request.whatCounselMustDecide: Does an administrative DOJ record-removal/update request have a waiting period at all, or should this route be bound no_waiting_period?

MT:marijuana-related-redesignation-expun.why: The MMRTA redesignation route's own prose describes Form A (currently serving) and Form B (sentence completed), service on the county attorney and a 21-day opposition window. It states no eligibility waiting period. The only bound durations reachable are the § 46-18-1104 five-year rows and the 30-day DOJ processing time, neither of which is MMRTA's.

candidatesConsidered.quote: no convictions … for five years after completing the sentence terms
DOJ says to allow about 30 days for processing.

MT:marijuana-related-redesignation-expun.whatCounselMustDecide: Does MMRTA redesignation/expungement under Mont. Code § 16-12-113 carry a waiting period, or is it available on completion of sentence with none?

MT:non-conviction-criminal-history-remov.why: The profile's own summary line for this route is 'Non-convictions CRISS removal/sealing under 44-5-202 process', with no period stated. The reachable bound durations are again the § 46-18-1104 five-year rows and the 30-day DOJ processing time. A non-conviction removal plausibly has no waiting period, but the profile does not say so, and inferring 'none' from silence is authoring just as much as inferring five years is.

candidatesConsidered.quote: Waiting period Generally 5 years after completing sentence terms
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: the same table line explicitly separates 'Non-convictions CRISS removal/sealing under 44-5-202 process' from the misdemeanor waiting period

MT:non-conviction-criminal-history-remov.whatCounselMustDecide: Does § 44-5-202 CRISS non-conviction removal carry a waiting period, or should it be bound no_waiting_period?

NC:nonviolent-conviction-expunction-unde.why: The profile publishes the full G.S. 15A-145.5 tier table with rule ids and durations, so the durations are not the problem — the SELECTOR is. The tier turns on TWO facts: whether the record is a misdemeanor or a felony, and how many nonviolent convictions the petitioner has. The flow asks offense_level, which narrows four tiers to two, and asks nothing that carries the conviction count. Choosing 3 over 7, or 10 over 20, for a participant whose count we never asked is a policy decision about unknowns, not a transcription.

tierTableFromTheProfile.quote: One nonviolent misdemeanor — after 3 years (reduced from 5 by the 2025 law, for petitions filed on/after 7/9/2025).
More than one nonviolent misdemeanor — after 7 years from the last conviction / completion of sentence.
One nonviolent felony — after 10 years from completion of the sentence.
Two or three nonviolent felonies — after 20 years; all nonviolent felonies disposed in the same session of court count as one.

NC:nonviolent-conviction-expunction-unde.theMissingFact: the number of nonviolent convictions the petitioner is seeking to clear, and whether any were disposed in the same session of court (wait-18: 'all nonviolent felonies disposed in a single session of court are treated as one nonviolent felony conviction for counting and waiting-period purposes')
NC:nonviolent-conviction-expunction-unde.whatCounselMustDecide: Either add a conviction-count fact to the flow so a conditional binding can be authored, or decide the disambiguation policy (for example longest_bound_duration within the offense_level branch) as a matter of legal safety.

NC:youthful-pre-raise-the-age-expunction.why: This route is G.S. 15A-145.8A. The only youth-specific duration the profile publishes is wait-11, 'Under-18 misdemeanor 15A-145 2 years Targeted statute' — a DIFFERENT statute (15A-145). Everything else reachable is the 15A-145.5 tier table, which is a different route again. Binding a 15A-145 duration to a 15A-145.8A route because both concern young people is exactly the kind of near-miss the binding table exists to stop.

candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: G.S. 15A-145, not the 15A-145.8A route this binding is for

NC:youthful-pre-raise-the-age-expunction.whatCounselMustDecide: What waiting period, if any, G.S. 15A-145.8A carries, and whether the profile should publish it as its own rule rather than leaving the route to borrow from 15A-145 or 15A-145.5.

NE:automatic-nonconviction-sealing.why: This is the closest any route in this shard comes to a clean conditional binding, and it still fails on one answer value. Three of the four case_outcome values that reach this route settle to a single published rule. The fourth does not: Nebraska's single option 'Diversion, deferred disposition, supervision, or similar program' merges completed diversion (two years, wait-02) with deferred judgment and problem-solving-court completion (immediate, wait-03). Two published rules, different durations, one answer value, and no fact in the flow separates them.

partialMappingThatDoesSettle.quote: Acquittal, qualifying dismissal, deferred judgment completion, or problem-solving-court completion: sealing is immediate upon agency notice.

partialMappingThatDoesSettle.answerValue: Dismissed, no-billed, nolle prosequi, or not prosecuted
partialMappingThatDoesSettle.quote: Acquittal, qualifying dismissal, deferred judgment completion, or problem-solving-court completion: sealing is immediate upon agency notice.

partialMappingThatDoesSettle.answerValue: Arrest or citation with no charge filed
partialMappingThatDoesSettle.quote: No charges filed after prosecutor decline: public access ends one year after arrest.

theConflict.answerValue: Diversion, deferred disposition, supervision, or similar program
quotes: No charges filed after completed diversion: public access ends two years after arrest.
Acquittal, qualifying dismissal, deferred judgment completion, or problem-solving-court completion: sealing is immediate upon agency notice.

NE:automatic-nonconviction-sealing.whatCounselMustDecide: Either split Nebraska's diversion answer value so completed diversion and deferred judgment are distinguishable, or state which rule governs when they are not. The other three values are ready to bind as written above.

NE:juvenile-automatic-sealing.why: The prose selector sees no waiting-period rule at all for this route. The one juvenile duration the profile publishes, wait-09 ('the juvenile, parent, or guardian may move once the juvenile reaches 18 or six months after case closure, whichever is sooner'), belongs to the PETITION BACKSTOP route — which already has an authored binding as NE:juvenile-petition-backstop — and describes when a petition may be filed, not when automatic sealing occurs. The route's own clauses say qualifying events 'can trigger automatic sealing' with no period.

candidatesConsidered.quote: If not automatically sealed, the juvenile, parent, or guardian may move once the juvenile reaches 18 or six months after case closure, whichever is sooner.
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: this rule is the backstop petition's, already bound to NE:juvenile-petition-backstop, and its own text begins 'If not automatically sealed'

NE:juvenile-automatic-sealing.whatCounselMustDecide: Does automatic juvenile sealing under §§ 43-2,108.01 to 43-2,108.05 run on a period, or on the qualifying event? If the latter, bind no_waiting_period.

NE:law-enforcement-error-expungement.why: No waiting-period rule in the Nebraska profile reaches this route, and the route's own clauses are entirely procedural: district court, county attorney as respondent, clear-and-convincing evidence of arresting-agency error. A waiting period for an arrest caused by law-enforcement error would be surprising, and § 29-3523(6) probably has none — but 'probably has none' is a legal conclusion and the profile does not state it. I cannot name a rule id, so no binding can be proposed.
NE:law-enforcement-error-expungement.whatCounselMustDecide: Confirm § 29-3523(6) carries no waiting period so the route can be bound no_waiting_period, or supply the rule.

NE:pardon-then-seal.why: The governing wait depends on one fact the participant already supplies — offense_level — and Nebraska's own profile publishes both branches with rule ids, quoted text and structured durations. Nothing is authored: both durations are already in the profile.

branches.quote: The source states a ten-year wait from final discharge for felony pardon applications and three years for misdemeanors, with later contact or conviction resetting the period.
Felony ten years, misdemeanor three years from discharge.

answerValuesDeliberatelyNotBound.why: The profile's own rule wait-16 states 'Out-of-state and federal convictions and traffic/DUI offenses are not eligible' for this route. Traffic is an ELIGIBILITY exclusion, not a waiting period, and belongs to the exclusion layer. 'I am not sure' should not silently pick a branch.

NE:pardon-then-seal.fidelityWarningForTheCaptain: Do NOT bind the felony branch to wait-07. wait-07's ruleText states both periods but its structured duration captured only the three-year misdemeanor figure. The ten-year felony duration is carried correctly by wait-16 and wait-19.
NE:pardon-then-seal.recommendedActiveNote: Not recommended ACTIVE. A proposal is not a binding; this route resolves through the provisional selector until the integration captain authors the binding.

NE:set-aside-incarceration-one-year-or-l.why: The two candidates conflict and neither is an eligibility waiting period. wait-04's two years is a DENIAL-RECENCY bar ('no set-aside denial may have occurred in the previous two years'), not a period the petitioner waits after completing their sentence. wait-15's structured duration of one year is a compile-time mis-capture: its text is 'Conviction, one year or less incarceration…', where 'one year' is the sentence-length ceiling that defines the route, not a wait.

candidatesConsidered.quote: The sentence must be complete, no charge may be pending, no sex-offender registration may be required, the offense cannot be vehicular homicide, and no set-aside denial may have occurred in the previous two years.
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: a bar on recent denials, not a waiting period from sentence completion

candidatesConsidered.quote: Conviction, one year or less incarceration, sentence complete, no pending charges, not SORA, not vehicular homicide, no set-aside denial in past two years: a set-aside path may exist under § 29-2264(3).
candidatesConsidered.rejectedBecause: the captured duration is the incarceration ceiling that defines route eligibility, not a wait

NE:set-aside-incarceration-one-year-or-l.whatCounselMustDecide: Does § 29-2264(3) require any elapsed period beyond sentence completion? If not, bind no_waiting_period and treat the two-year denial bar as an exclusion rule rather than a waiting rule.

NE:set-aside-probation-fine-community-se.why: No waiting-period rule reaches this route. Its clauses are completion conditions, not timing: sentence conditions satisfactorily completed, fine paid, community service completed, discretionary decision on best-interest and public-welfare factors. I cannot name a rule id, so no binding can be proposed. OR:marijuana-specific-set-aside-redesign.why: Oregon's marijuana route works by RECLASSIFYING a pre-1 July 2015 marijuana offence to the level it would carry today, and only then applying the ordinary class-based tier. So the governing rule depends on the reclassified offence class and on the offence date — and the flow asks neither. Oregon's offense_level offers Misdemeanor, Felony, Infraction or violation, Traffic or driving matter and Municipal or ordinance matter; none of these is a statutory class, and no question carries the pre/post-July-2015 fact.

boundedAttemptMade.what: src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/AZ-arizona.json#questions[court] rebound from type `text` to type `single_choice` with a four-option controlled list drawn from Arizona's own filing-destination source text.

boundedAttemptMade.note: One attempt, on one question, in one jurisdiction. The verifier's assertion is structural and applies identically to every question in every one of the 51 compiled profiles, so repeating it per state would produce the same failure 13 more times without adding information.

browserEnvironmentAttempt.what: One bounded attempt to run the crawl acceptance tests: npm run dev, then EXPAI_FLOW_AUDIT_JURISDICTIONS=AZ node tests/e2e/expungement-ai/flow-audit/crawl-screening-flows.mjs with EXPAI_FLOW_AUDIT_CHROMIUM pointed at the container's chromium-1194 build.

browserEnvironmentAttempt.secondFailure: The crawl launches, navigates and captures, but every terminal screenshot shows the screening card stuck on 'Loading your state's questions...'. A separate minimal Playwright probe against the same origin confirmed it: after 30 seconds the body still reads 'Loading your state's questions...', with 0 failed requests and no page error — only Next dev HMR websocket noise. GET /api/expungement-ai/profiles/arizona answers 200 in 1.3s from the same container, so the data is served and the client never leaves its loading state.
browserEnvironmentAttempt.matchesPhase2: Phase 2 recorded exactly this, and recorded that the PRODUCT BASE source served the same way behaves identically. It is a property of the environment, not of any correction.
browserEnvironmentAttempt.evidence: loading-state terminal screenshots for both AZ flows, desktop and mobile, written outside the tree

sharedPathsAndControlsRequired.control: Roger's authorisation. scripts/verify-expungement-plain-language-values.mjs pins each approved question by sha256 over its canonical JSON, so the entry must carry the exact post-change bytes.
sharedPathsAndControlsRequired.why: the only sanctioned exemption from the type/options/required/contextOnly parity assertion

the switch has branches for single_choice, multi_select, yes_no_*, text, text_or_unknown, date_or_unknown and number_or_range. There is no selector-with-manual-entry branch, so 'a state-aware selector with a clearly-labelled manual entry fallback' cannot be rendered by configuration alone.

FALLBACK_PACKET_QUESTIONS defines county and court as text_or_unknown for any jurisdiction whose profile does not define them. The compiled-profile definition wins where present, so this file does not block the rebind — but it must agree, or a state without the question falls back to free text.

sharedPathsAndControlsRequired.control: Roger — TEST_COUNTY_AND_COURT_DATA_SOURCE, an owner-supplied programme input that was never supplied
sharedPathsAndControlsRequired.why: the controlled county dataset UX-COUNTY-001 requires. detect-static-defects.mjs checks for this exact path.

normalizeQuestionOptions coerces any non-array options to null. A selector's option list must survive projection to reach the browser; it will, because it is a non-empty string array, but the projection is where a malformed list becomes silent free text.
for the related CA blocker only: ambiguityReason escalates on an explicit-unknown answer to any rendered prepay question without scoping to the matched route.
